dedupe_keys.name: urban river restoration and blue green network in łodz sokołowka river

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Łódź, Poland, whose rivers were canalised and culverted during nineteenth-century industrialisation, restored the Sokołówka river using ecohydrology as the pilot of a city-wide Blue-Green Network for stormwater management. Within the EU SWITCH project (2006-2011) the river was re-engineered with three stormwater reservoirs (2006-2010) and a patented sequential sedimentation and biofiltration system (2011), and a Learning Alliance brought together city departments, researchers and regional and national stakeholders; the Arturówek reservoirs were then rehabilitated in the LIFE EH-REK project (2010-2015), and a Sokołówka park plan was approved in 2016. The SWITCH budget in Łódź was about 1.15 million euros, including about 700,000 euros for the river demonstration and 130,000 euros for the Learning Alliance, plus in-kind research. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the city and LIFE project pages. Caveats: the success owed much to EU project funding, and quantitative hazard reduction is not reported. It illustrates nature-based stormwater and flood hazard reduction and climate adaptation in a dense city; related records are the Isar-Plan, Augustenborg and Gomeznarro Park case studies.
name: Urban river restoration and Blue-Green Network in Łódź (Sokołówka river)
organisations: European Regional Centre for Ecohydrology of the Polish Academy of Sciences
outcomes: The Sokołówka pilot convinced the city and water professionals to replicate ecohydrological river restoration elsewhere in Łódź and led to follow-up reservoir and park projects.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the SWITCH project, City of Łódź, University of Łódź and the European Regional Centre for Ecohydrology
